(i) ERM models do not generalize as predicted by existing theory; (ii) ERM models generalize better when they have higher Fisher information, lower predictive entropy, and lower MMD; and (iii) ERM models trained using the cross-entropy loss are not the best at generalizing out-of-distribution

(1) the domain adaptation theory of (Ben-David et al., 2007) does not provide a good explanation for the out-of-domain performance of ERM models, (2) the out-of-domain accuracy of ERM models is correlated with measures relating to the maximum mean discrepancy, the Fisher information, and predictive entropy, and (3) the correlation between out-of-domain accuracy and these measures is higher for ERM models that have been trained with a larger batch size.
